questions.contextText:
Directions for Questions 96 to 100:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:
"The resilience of democratic institutions depends not merely on codified statutory frameworks, but upon the
unwritten norms of civic restraint and institutional forbearance. When political contenders view adversaries not as
legitimate opponents but as existential enemies, constitutional checks turn into partisan instruments. Historical
precedents across diverse civilizations reveal that legal mechanisms alone cannot prevent authoritarian drift once
mutual toleration erodes. A thriving democracy requires an active citizenry that values institutional integrity over
ephemeral electoral triumphs, guarding the norms that sustain fair governance."
questions.questionText: According to the author, what is indispensable alongside codified statutes for democratic resilience?
options: Unwritten norms of civic restraint and institutional forbearance
